title: Industrial Lease (Net): Kestrel Flats Logistics Park, Building 3, Unit B
fictional_notice: All parties and facts are invented.

defects.title: 20 percent month-to-month rent increases on 30 days' notice
defects.why: During the month-to-month tenancy the landlord may raise base rent by 20 percent, more than once a year, on 30 days' notice. The lease recites that the tenant is a qualified commercial tenant, so an increase of more than 10 percent over the prior 12 months needs at least 90 days' written notice.
quotes: Lessor may increase the Base Rent for the month-to-month tenancy by twenty percent (20%) over the Base Rent then being paid, and may do so more than once in any year, by giving Lessee thirty (30) days' written notice

defects.title: Deposit refund clock runs from landlord's completion of restoration work
defects.why: The refund is due 30 days after the later of surrender and the date the landlord finishes any move-out work the tenant left undone, so the landlord can hold the deposit well past 30 days after it has possession. The deposit must be returned no later than 30 days from the date the landlord receives possession.
quotes: within thirty (30) days after the later of (a) the date Lessee surrenders possession of the Premises to Lessor and (b) the date on which Lessor has completed all repair, restoration and removal work

defects.title: No statutory CASp notice after stating premises were not inspected
defects.why: The lease says the premises have not had a Certified Access Specialist inspection and then goes straight to cost allocation. Where no disability access inspection certificate has been issued, the lease must include the statutory CASp notice paragraph, and it does not.
quotes: The Premises have not undergone inspection by a Certified Access Specialist.

defects.title: Section 1951.4 remedy with an absolute ban on assignment and subletting
defects.why: The lease flatly prohibits any assignment or sublease and says the landlord need not consider a request, yet it also invokes the section 1951.4 remedy of keeping the lease in effect after abandonment. That remedy is available only if the tenant may sublet or assign subject at most to reasonable standards or consent not unreasonably withheld.
quotes: shall not sublet all or any part of the Premises, and shall not permit any other person or organization to occupy or share the Premises, and Lessor is not required to consider or respond to any request for consent to do so
Lessor may hold Lessee to this Lease for as long as Lessor does not terminate Lessee's right to possession, and may sue for each installment of Rent when it falls due

defects.title: Operating expenses may include costs up to 36 months before the start date, however old
defects.why: The operating expense schedule lets the landlord bill any unbilled cost incurred at any time in the term or in the 36 months before it began, regardless of age. For a qualified commercial tenant the costs must have been incurred in the prior 18 months or be reasonably expected in the next 12.
quotes: incurred at any time during the Lease Term or during the thirty-six (36) months before the Start Date and has not previously billed to an occupant of the Premises, without regard to how long ago the cost was incurred

defects.title: Pre-dispute jury waiver in the guaranty
defects.why: The guaranty schedule has the guarantor waive a jury for any claim under the guaranty or the lease and agree to a bench trial, before any dispute exists. A jury may be waived only in the ways listed in subdivision (f), and a pre-dispute contract clause is not one of them.
quotes: Guarantor irrevocably waives, to the extent the law allows, any right to have a jury decide any claim, defense or counterclaim arising under this Guaranty or the Lease, and agrees that any such matter will be tried by a judge sitting without a jury.

defects.title: $1,000 per trailer per day liquidated damages in the park rules
defects.why: A park rule charges $1,000 per trailer for each day or part of a day a trailer is outside its assigned stall, with no notice or chance to move it. A fixed sum of that size for a parking infraction may bear no reasonable relation to any loss the landlord could have expected when the lease was made.
quotes: the occupant shall pay Lessor $1,000 per trailer for each day or part of a day, as liquidated damages, which Lessor may add to the next installment of Rent without prior notice or an opportunity to move the trailer
